extracted.intended_audience: Small businesses applying to Army SBIR awards and the Army SBIR proposal evaluators
extracted.subtask_description: Official evaluation criteria and scoring guidance for Army SBIR proposals (Phase I, Phase II, and Direct-to-Phase-II). Describes sections to be addressed in proposals, weights, explanatory text, and four-level scoring descriptors for each dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: INTRODUCTION
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a clear, concise description of what your innovation does or will do, and where you are in your evolution. Make clear its intended impact on the Army. Evaluators should 'get it' after reading this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Weights shown on page: weight 5% (Phase I), weight 2% (Direct-to-Phase-II and Phase II). Scoring guidance (Superior scale):
- Unsatisfactory: Ineffective introduction. Failed to provide concise innovation proposition.
- Marginal: Adequate introduction. Gradually conveyed innovation's purpose and value. Should be more crisp.
- Satisfactory: Effective introduction. Systematically conveys innovation's purpose and value.
- Superior: Exceptional introduction. Immediately conveys innovation's purpose and value.
Evaluator expectation: be concise, immediately clear what the innovation is and its maturity. Anti-patterns: vague, long-winded introductions that fail to state the core proposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPERATIONAL IMPACT
rubrics_metrics.description: At the scale of a single Army end-user, argue that their jobs or lives will be significantly improved if your solution is adopted. What is the impact of your solution for a soldier/Army civilian vs. today's solutions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Appears under 'Potential for Army Impact'. Weights on page: weight 25% (Phase I), weight 20% (Phase II/Direct-to-Phase-II variations exist). Scoring guidance:
- If successful, no improvement vs. existing technological approaches.
- If successful, slight improvement vs. existing technological approaches.
- If successful, significant improvement vs. existing technological approaches.
- If successful, radical improvement vs. existing technological approaches.
Evaluator expectation: describe measurable, user-level improvements relative to current solutions and focus on the end-user impact. Anti-patterns: claims about broad benefits without concrete end-user impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: POTENTIAL SCALE OF IMPACT
rubrics_metrics.description: Here, we're looking for an idea of how broad the impact you described above could be. Look into the future to a time when your solution is both technically mature and actively in use by Army personnel. Describe the scale and scope of your impact within the context of the Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Appears under 'Potential for Army Impact'. Scoring guidance for mature, fully deployed solution:
- A fully deployed, mature solution could impact only niche use cases.
- A fully deployed, mature solution could impact an Army element.
- A fully deployed, mature solution could impact several Army elements.
- A fully deployed, mature solution could have impact across the entire Army.
Evaluator expectation: articulate long-term adoption scenarios and describe which parts of the Army would be affected. Avoid conflating desirable impact with likely implementation constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCIENTIFIC FEASIBILITY
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the science behind the solution sound? Convince readers who don't have deep expertise in your field that your innovation is built atop sound scientific and engineering principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Appears under 'Technical Feasibility'. Scoring guidance:
- No scientific basis for presented approach.
- Incomplete scientific basis for presented approach.
- Credible scientific basis for presented approach.
- Convincing scientific basis for presented approach.
Evaluator expectation: clearly explain underlying scientific principles, cite evidence, and make the case for feasibility to non-specialist evaluators. Anti-patterns: unsupported assertions of novel science or hand-wavy descriptions without citations or prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: ENABLING TECHNOLOGIES
rubrics_metrics.description: Point to the foundational technologies that you rely on to deliver your solution. Do the required enabling technologies introduce added risk? Using proven (and ideally Army-fielded) underlying technologies and techniques helps to lower technical risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Appears under 'Technical Feasibility'. Scoring guidance (technology readiness/risk):
- Requires nonexistent or unavailable technology.
- Requires emerging, cutting edge technology.
- Requires proven technologies.
- Requires Army-fielded technologies.
Evaluator expectation: list dependencies and assess their maturity and availability. Discuss whether enabling tech is commercial, emerging, or already Army-fielded. Anti-patterns: hiding key dependencies or assuming availability of unproven components.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALTERNATIVE TECHNICAL APPROACHES
rubrics_metrics.description: From a technologist's perspective, why is your proposed solution the best choice for the Army? Refute the alternative engineering approaches others are using. Why does your technology win?
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Appears under 'Technical Feasibility'. Scoring guidance:
- No examination of alternatives.
- Partially refutes alternatives.
- Adequately refutes alternatives.
- Persuasively refutes alternatives.
Evaluator expectation: acknowledge competing approaches, explain tradeoffs, and justify selection of your approach. Anti-patterns: claiming superiority without comparative analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: TECHNICAL RISK MITIGATION
rubrics_metrics.description: No matter your current technology readiness level, technical risks remain. Identify those risks. Present a credible plan to tackle those risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears under 'Technical Feasibility'. Expectation: identify key technical risks, provide mitigation strategies, contingency plans, and realistic timelines. While explicit four-level wording isn't always repeated, related scoring appears in Technical/Transition tables (e.g., appropriateness of next steps). Anti-patterns: failing to acknowledge major technical obstacles or offering implausible mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARMY TRANSITION PATHWAY
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning for success, what's next for you after this SBIR award? Describe the next type of deal you aim to make with the Army, e.g. a CRADA, a different SBIR contract, a CSO, etc. Briefly outline your current plan to unlock that next opportunity and/or share the biggest risks you see post this SBIR award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Appears under 'Transition'. Weights shown vary (weight 25% / 20% in different documents). Scoring guidance:
- Fails to identify next contract goal and/or fails to present a plan for near-term execution.
- Identifies next contract goal. Has a plan for near-term execution.
- Identifies stage-appropriate next contract goal. Credible plan for near-term execution.
- Identifies ideal next contract goal. Convincing plan for near-term execution.
Evaluator expectation: show realistic, staged plans for transition into Army use, including target contract vehicles and engagement strategy. Anti-patterns: vague or unrealistic post-SBIR plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR MILESTONE SCHEDULE
rubrics_metrics.description: Please share with us a thoughtful execution plan. Strike a balance between giving us a sense of the detailed thinking behind the scenes and the need for your contracting officer to manage a reasonably small number of milestones during your period of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Appears under 'Transition' or project execution sections. Scoring guidance:
- Unclear or non-credible project milestones, or timing.
- Mostly clear, credible project milestones and timing. Mostly appropriate level of detail.
- Mostly clear, credible project milestones and timing. Appropriate level of detail. (some variations across versions)
- Completely clear, credible project milestones and timing. Appropriate level of detail.
Evaluator expectation: provide clear, stage-appropriate milestones with credible timing and deliverables. Anti-patterns: overly granular or implausible milestone schedules, or too few milestones to monitor progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIRM SURVIVAL RISK / FIRM CASH FLOW
rubrics_metrics.description: SBIR funds are meant to fuel growth rather than stave off a firm's impending financial failure. Demonstrate that your company will survive financially as a going concern through the early stages of a Phase III contract, sometimes referred to as 'transitioning' into use by Army personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Appears under 'Transition' financial considerations. Scoring guidance:
- Fails to demonstrate solvency through a Phase III.
- Marginally demonstrates solvency through a Phase III.
- Credibly demonstrates solvency through a Phase III.
- Convincingly demonstrates solvency through a Phase III.
Evaluator expectation: present realistic cash-flow projections, burn-rate assumptions, and paths to bridge to Phase III. Anti-patterns: relying solely on SBIR funds without credible follow-on funding or revenue plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: OTHER PEOPLE'S MONEY
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the case that non-Army and/or non-DoD dollars will continue to fund improvements to your solution from which the Army will benefit in the future. Companies who cannot demonstrate non-Army and/or non-DoD funding sources for future solution enhancements are less attractive to the Applied SBIR program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Weight entries show this often under Transition with weight 10%–15% depending on track. Scoring guidance:
- Fails to present non-DoD sources for future R&D funding.
- Evolving non-DoD sources of future R&D funding.
- Secure non-DoD source(s) of future R&D funding.
- Diverse and robust non-DoD sources of future R&D funding.
Evaluator expectation: show letters of interest, partner commitments, commercial customers, VC, or other non-DoD funding paths. Anti-patterns: claiming likely commercial interest without evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: FINANCIAL PROFIT POTENTIAL
rubrics_metrics.description: Through the Applied SBIR program, the Army wants to take advantage of the speed and scalability of dual-use companies. Make your best case that your product is or will be profitable. If you have more than one product, please focus your argument on the product / solution presented for this SBIR program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Appears with weight typically 10%–15% across documents. Scoring guidance:
- Product does not have a path to profitability.
- Demonstrates product has a path to profitability.
- Demonstrates product progressing toward profitability.
- Demonstrates product has achieved profitability.
Evaluator expectation: present business model, revenue drivers, unit economics, and route to profit. Anti-patterns: focusing on abstract market potential without unit economics or go-to-market plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: TEAM ABILITY
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove your team has executed well as a group. Please draw clear distinctions between private sector, DoD and civilian government work. What milestones have you accomplished as a group in this company?
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Appears with weight ~10%. Scoring guidance:
- Evidence of marginal group execution.
- Evidence of some group execution.
- Evidence of impressive group execution.
- Evidence of exceptional group execution.
Evaluator expectation: clarify roles, relevant past performance, complementary skills, and documented accomplishments as a team. Anti-patterns: incomplete bios, unclear responsibilities, or overstating past outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: QUALITY OF PROSE (SUBMISSION QUALITY)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove you write clearly. Prove you argue convincingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Appears under 'Submission Quality' with weight typically 3%–5%. Scoring guidance:
- Poorly written. Very difficult to impossible to follow argument. Several spelling or grammar errors.
- Moderately written. Sometimes difficult to follow argument. A few spelling / grammar errors.
- Effectively written. Convincing, easy to follow argument. No spelling or grammar errors.
- Clearly and persuasively written. Compelling arguments. No spelling or grammar errors. (phase tables also show 'Persuasively supported by meaningful data' adjacent to data quality)
Evaluator expectation: produce a clear, well-edited proposal with logical flow. Anti-patterns: grammar/spelling errors, unclear argument structure, or unsupported claims reducing credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: DATA QUALITY & ATTRIBUTION
rubrics_metrics.description: Support your arguments with relevant, properly attributed data to enhance your credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Appears under 'Submission Quality' with weight typically 3%–5%. Scoring guidance:
- Poorly supported by data. Little to no data attribution.
- Partially supported by data. Some data attribution.
- Credibly supported by data. Adequate data attribution.
- Persuasively supported by meaningful data. Comprehensive data attribution.
Evaluator expectation: include relevant data, cite sources, and ensure data are appropriate and trustworthy. Anti-patterns: using unattributed statistics, cherry-picked data, or weak evidence.
